description: Average aCL IgG and ANA over all matched examination records within each sex. Each examination counts once.

a.request: For each patient sex (`Patient.SEX`), use every examination record that matches a patient (drop examinations with no matching patient), with each examination counting once even when a patient has several. Give the sex, the average `aCL IgG`, the average `ANA`, and that sex's average ANA divided by the mean of the per-sex average ANA values. Ignore missing values in all averages and don't round.
a.sql:
WITH matched AS (
  SELECT p.SEX, e.`aCL IgG`, e.ANA
  FROM Examination AS e
  INNER JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = e.ID
), sex_averages AS (
  SELECT SEX, AVG(`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(ANA) AS avg_ana
  FROM matched
  GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT SEX, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana,
       avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM sex_averages) AS normalized_avg_ana
FROM sex_averages;

c.request: By patient sex, what are the average aCL IgG and ANA values in the examination data (only examinations linked to a patient, missing values ignored)? Also give each sex's average ANA as a ratio of the mean of the per-sex ANA averages, unrounded. Average aCL IgG and ANA over all matched examination records within each sex. Each examination counts once.
c.sql:
WITH sex_averages AS (
  SELECT p.SEX,
         AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg,
         AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
  FROM Examination AS e
  JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = e.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
)
SELECT SEX,
       avg_acl_igg,
       avg_ana,
       avg_ana / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_ratio
FROM sex_averages;

b.request: For each patient sex, report the average aCL IgG and ANA across all examination records linked to a patient of that sex, counting each examination once and ignoring missing values; also report that sex’s average ANA divided by the unweighted mean of the per-sex ANA averages, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.SEX,
        AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg,
        AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Examination AS e ON e.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    avg_acl_igg,
    avg_ana,
    avg_ana / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_average_ratio
FROM sex_averages;

d.request: By patient sex, what are the average aCL IgG and ANA values across all examination records linked to a patient, counting each examination once and ignoring missing values? Also, express each sex’s average ANA as a ratio of the mean of the per-sex ANA averages, without rounding.
d.sql:
WITH sex_averages AS (
  SELECT p.SEX,
         AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg,
         AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
  FROM Examination AS e
  JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = e.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
)
SELECT SEX,
       avg_acl_igg,
       avg_ana,
       avg_ana / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_average_ratio
FROM sex_averages;
